page: Microsoft Azure E8d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 35 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. In addition to general virtualization, the instance includes 322 GB of bundled local SSD storage. No discrete graphics processors are attached.

Benchmark data reflects mid-tier compute and memory throughput alongside standard per-thread limitations. The instance achieves average ratings on multi-core metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 8,541.35 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 7,432.24. PassMark database operations hit 2,917.65 and Redis SET throughput measures 6.53 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core processing scores lower, with Geekbench single-core at 1,064.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1,410.98. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 28.37 GB/sec, while cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaches 413.99 GB/sec. Complex LLM inference tasks exhibit poor token generation throughput on medium-sized models, reflecting reliance on CPU execution without hardware accelerators.

The E8d_v4 provides cost efficiency for memory-dense architectures by pairing substantial RAM and temporary local scratch disk directly on the node without the overhead of GPU provisioning. Its 8 GB per vCPU footprint makes it suitable for enterprise relational databases, in-memory caches like Redis, data warehousing staging nodes, and standard corporate application servers requiring high memory headroom.
description: Microsoft Azure E8d_v4 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 322 GB of local SSD temporary storage, operating without dedicated GPUs on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is designed around an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, catering to memory-intensive workloads. Performance evaluations demonstrate average capabilities across multi-threaded operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 8,541.35, PassMark database score of 2,917.65, and Redis SET throughput of 6.53 million operations per second. However, single-core execution metrics and uncached large-block memory bandwidth test on the lower end. With its generous memory pool and bundled high-speed local disk, the E8d_v4 fits production relational databases, in-memory data structures, ETL staging environments, and caching layers that prioritize high capacity over intense per-core compute.
